title: The Glorious Doctrine of Adoption
speaker: Elder Nick Anderson

outline.title: The Context of Adoption in the Order of Salvation
subpoints: Adoption follows justification in the Ordo Salutis
Immediate and irrevocable status upon faith in Christ
Comparison to Greco-Roman legal adoption: full rights, erasure of past, secure status

outline.title: Benefit 1: Deriving a New Nature from God
subpoints: Partakers of the divine nature through the Spirit
Restoration of spiritual life lost in the Fall
Contrast between the old nature (bondage to sin) and new nature (ability to live holy lives)

outline.title: Benefit 2: Obtaining a New Name
subpoints: Called children of God and Christians
Prophetic fulfillment of being named by the Lord

outline.title: Benefit 3: Receiving the Spirit of Adoption
subpoints: Freedom from guilt, legal bondage, and fear of death
The Spirit calms anxiety and enables confident prayer

outline.title: Benefit 4: Access to the Throne of Grace with Boldness
subpoints: Entering the holiest by the blood of Jesus
Prayer characterized by childlike trust rather than fear
Assurance based on Christ's intercession, not personal merit

summary:
This lesson continues the series on the Westminster Confession of Faith, focusing on Chapter 12: Adoption. The teaching situates adoption within the Ordo Salutis, noting that it occurs immediately upon justification and is an irrevocable status. By drawing parallels to Greco-Roman legal adoption, the sermon highlights the full legal rights, erasure of past debts, and secure status that believers enjoy as children of God.

The primary text, Romans 8:15-17, is used to explore the benefits of adoption. The first benefit discussed is the derivation of a new nature from God. While believers do not become divine in essence, they partake in the divine nature through the Holy Spirit, enabling them to live holy lives in contrast to their previous bondage to sin. This transformation is described as a restoration of spiritual life lost in the Fall.

Subsequent benefits include receiving a new name, being called children of God and Christians, and receiving the Spirit of Adoption. This Spirit frees believers from the fear of death and legal guilt, transforming their character and enabling obedience. The lesson concludes by discussing the bold access to the throne of grace that this status provides. Believers are encouraged to pray with confidence and childlike trust, relying on the intercession of Christ rather than their own merit, as God invites them to draw near to Him.
